HyperFrames v0.8.190

Released on 2026-10-23.

Motion blur now picks a cheaper way to draw when it can, and renders use less memory. Studio gains a preview seek bar, and an idle editor stops waking the GPU.

Features

  • Automatic tier, 240°/32 defaults, check finding, and Studio stops opting out (79b57ab12, #6108).
  • Core: Capture blur falls back to per-element filters where capture cannot run (4ed781338, #6107).
  • Studio: Add a preview seek bar (2512642d0, #6103).

Fixes

  • Engine: The BeginFrame start-up check waits for the first frame up to its deadline (73718a251, #6149).
  • Engine: A render no longer decodes the videos it replaces with extracted frames (01a523bcf, #6142).
  • CLI: Render -c takes an absolute entry inside the project, relative to the project (9fe0511c2, #6141).
  • Engine: The video frame cache budget is shared by the capture workers (f8ae1483c, #6135).
  • Studio: The thumbnail capture page loads media near the playhead like the preview (28ac4d76b, #6146).
  • Engine: A long audio mix prepares its clips a few at a time (1dc97921c, #6132).

Performance

  • Studio: An idle editor stops waking the GPU four times a second (6ad7c82d2, #6109).
  • AWS Lambda: Warm the audio function while the plan runs (fb2f7c1a8, #6148).

item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.188

Released on 2026-10-23.

Lambda cloud renders now run their video work on arm64 by default, which costs less per render. Pass --video-arch x86_64 to keep x86.

This release also fixes renders in folders with a percent sign, long renders with small frames, scripts that shadow console, and motion blur, audio timing and frame handling.

Features

  • CLI: Lambda deploy renders on arm64 by default, and --video-arch x86_64 keeps x86 (504ec2b30, #6073).
  • AWS Lambda: Push a prebuilt image to ECR without Docker (0df088926, #6063).
  • AWS Lambda: Attach the arm64 video image to releases and pin it (8d562a3d9, #6070).
  • AWS Lambda: Arm64 video function image from the handler ZIP (f6cbf87cd, #6064).
  • AWS Lambda: Run chunks on an optional arm64 image function (03ed14615, #6065).
  • CLI: Preserve page motion blur off in local renders (10c724bf5, #6081).

Fixes

  • Producer: A blank media src is no source instead of the page itself (c4c1e621d, #6121).
  • AWS Lambda: Keep the arm64 image staging script out of the published package (401d0655f, #6118).
  • Runtime: A composition script that shadows console no longer breaks the render runtime (b6de25391, #6119).
  • Producer: Long renders with small frames no longer fail the up-front disk estimate (aeecf3834, #6117).
  • Engine: Render into a folder whose name holds a percent sign (69738b7ce, #6116).
  • Lint: Tell an agent where to move a video nested in a timed wrapper (d1aeb31bf, #6113).
  • Core: Capture blur strobing, backdrop box, glow drop-out and callback motion (e85f56e86, #6106).
  • Core: A scene paints no filter output from an HTML layer before its start or after its end (025549391, #6097).
  • Engine: Hundreds of effects in one audio group mix in time, and a mix timeout is named (1accb709f, #6101).
  • AWS Lambda: Make webm and mov audio in the separate audio task like mp4 (f5f884e33, #6098).
  • Preserve motion blur off through cloud render requests (622527117, #6087).
  • CLI: Preserve video frames when scenes reuse element IDs (da6b77bd8, #6095).
  • Audio: Fit PCM to video frames before AAC delivery (9da107aef, #6089).
  • Engine: Publish video frames only after decoding (aa4b53533, #6092).
  • Parsers: Preserve Unicode offsets when stamping IDs (1cf4975d2, #6079).
  • Exclude base-marked generated files from comment checks (36c4a9fd8, #6091).
  • AWS Lambda: Retry a file upload after a dropped connection (77394fe9e, #6082).
  • Data-volume multiplies the volume lane in preview and render (a8ac55dc3, #6068).
  • Ci: Pin and reuse the docs validation CLI (27b9f6850, #6080).
  • Hooks: Run the checkout's own oxfmt, oxlint and tsc instead of bunx (b3f586903, #5751).
  • Studio: The edit-accuracy gate says the shards did not run, not that accuracy fell (609ff5a7c, #6069).

Docs & Examples

  • Guide and skill note for opt-in capture motion blur (4a788583f, #6049).
  • CLI: Document every command, and check it in CI (1b1a576d5, #5938).
  • Install the Studio app on Linux from the .deb (29643c7c8, #5946).
  • Send docs pageviews to the HyperFrames PostHog project (32ab255f6, #5948).

Internal

  • CLI: Process tests stop owning old processes that carry a reused parent pid on Windows (784e1d01d, #6111).
  • Studio: Retain Chrome launch diagnostics (821003b11, #6077).
  • Windows: Fail a hung engine-cli test step at its deadline and name the stuck process (1d0a18c81, #6100).
  • AWS Lambda: Pinned native ffmpeg build for an arm64 Lambda image (bb19f342d, #6062).
  • Mark cloud SDK output as generated (807803a45, #6088).
  • Help agents find hyperframes on npm and context7 (3d67fb9d1, #5937).
  • Studio: Sample gesture replay from one preview state (3dd9f5178, #6076).

Full changelog

  • CLI: Init --video frames the project to the clip's shape, so nothing is cropped (86b90bb42, #5984).
  • Core: A clip's volume lane stays smooth in preview while the page is busy (cfff4493d, #6057).

item.title: v0.8.185
item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.185

Released on 2026-10-21.

hyperframes cloud render --resolution 4k now works for transparent MOV and WebM. A render no longer fails when its audio peak stalls under correction, check accepts projects that inline the GSAP library, and cloud render chunks start their capture browsers while video frames extract. Capture motion blur arrives as an opt-in on the composition root.

Features

  • CLI: cloud render --resolution 4k accepts --format mov and --format webm; the CLI and the render server no longer refuse 4K with a transparent format (25126bca6, #6045).
  • Core: Capture motion blur: data-motion-blur on the composition root blurs fast-moving elements across sub-frame samples, with shutter angle and sample count settings (0f1d6908f, #5967); it follows the render's device scale, so 2x and 4K renders blur at full resolution (ffcef8f88, #5968).

Fixes

  • Producer: A render whose AAC true peak stalls above the limit during correction no longer fails at assemble (32ebdde61, #6043).
  • Lint: check no longer fails a project that pastes the GSAP library inline, and a bundle around GSAP never inherits its exemption (50e7e8df6, #6018).
  • Engine: A capture browser whose BeginFrame probe passed keeps BeginFrame capture when closing the probe page is slow (a8b576d15, #6037).

Performance

  • Producer: A cloud render chunk starts its capture browsers while its video frames are still being extracted, so heavy chunks finish sooner and cost less (0716670fa, #6031).

Full changelog

item.title: v0.8.184
item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.184

Released on 2026-10-21.

hyperframes cloud render now takes projects whose media is far larger than the project upload limit. Multi-worker mp4 renders start encoding while they capture, Lambda chunks run more capture browsers at once, and a heavy project's preview builds faster. Transparent webm keeps its transparency in Studio previews, and a color grade applies to an image that appears after its scene starts hidden.

Features

  • CLI: cloud render uploads media of 5 MB or more as hosted assets before zipping the project, so projects with media far larger than the upload limit render with no manual step. Uploads are cached, so a re-render sends only new or changed media (b306438e8, #5931).

Fixes

  • Studio Server: A transparent VP8 or VP9 webm, such as remove-background output, keeps its transparency in the preview copy that check, Studio and publish make (d67e81c7f, #6025).
  • Core: A color-graded image renders graded in snapshot and render when it is hidden as its scene starts and revealed later (087451837, #6012).
  • CLI: A preview refused inside a host app no longer stops other Chrome processes left behind by earlier runs (5641a9179, #6022).

Performance

  • Producer: A multi-worker mp4 render starts encoding while its frames are still being captured, instead of after, with byte-identical output (eec3c51d7, #5952).
  • AWS Lambda: Each chunk renders with as many capture browsers as the function can host, five instead of three on a 10 GB function, so heavy 4K chunks finish sooner (cde21630e, #6026).
  • Core: A heavy project's first preview page builds sooner, without rescanning its styles once per composition variable (0d51eb0de, #5893).
  • Core: A page build reads fonts, inlined assets and scenes mounted many times only once, and an offline build with a warm font cache makes no network request (884d8690a, #5954).

Internal

  • Core: The building blocks of capture motion blur (element poses, finding fast movers, the per-frame draw). Nothing uses them yet (8df2d8d95, #5875).
  • CLI: The capture network tests no longer flake on CI (cfdddd8a9, #6024).
  • A hung Windows test run keeps its log, and commit hooks lint .mjs and .cjs files (2e1cf69e0, #6023).

Full changelog

item.title: v0.8.183
item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.183

Released on 2026-10-21.

v0.8.182 was tagged but never reached npm (its publish stopped at the package size check), so everything listed for it ships in this release.

Website capture now handles pages that reload after a cookie banner, CLI commands start faster, a repeat check starts with the CLI and Chrome already up, and snapshot and check wait for late images as render does. Renders inside a macOS sandbox no longer fail, a sharp sound at a film's start no longer grows louder with each audio pass, and lambda sites create takes source files over 5 GB. Cloud renders mix their audio beside the chunks and fail loudly when an audio read is cut off, a 4K camera shown small reaches Chrome near the size it is drawn, a finished capture exits even when a site's DNS never answers, and an unreadable frame fails a render instead of shortening it.

Features

  • AWS Lambda: A cloud render mixes its audio on its own Lambda while the chunks render, instead of before them, so a long film finishes sooner (dee8380d2, #5997).
  • Producer: A cloud plan can leave its audio out and build that track on its own, which the Lambda change above uses (8b410f1cb, #5988).
  • Registry: New echo-smear component: a streak of copies that trails an element as a GSAP timeline moves it faster (23e7a384b, #5980).

Fixes

  • CLI: Website capture waits for a page that reloads after its cookie banner closes, so assets and scroll screenshots are no longer empty (0693839b5, #4949).
  • CLI: check prints progress while it makes browser-playable copies of phone videos (b7fa007bf, #5953).
  • CLI: check, snapshot and Studio show accented and non-Latin project text correctly instead of garbled (6d357ff0d, #5843).
  • CLI: check no longer calls a film static when it moves only through an SVG mask or clip path, a stroke reveal or a canvas (0bd626825, #5960).
  • CLI: check audits a color-graded video as the video it shows, so the video's layout opt-outs apply and its footage is not read as cut-off text (9f793a6db, #5963).
  • CLI: A scoped keepsMoving check ignores a changing page background outside its scope (ba1fa8b12, #5966).
  • Lint: check and lint place each scene's audio at its host's start, so scenes that play one after another no longer warn of overlapping audio (18207de1c, #6005).
  • CLI: The Chrome the CLI launches exits with it, even when the CLI is killed (434ad8c41, #5943).

item.title: v0.8.156
item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.156

Released on 2026-10-14.

Videos from screen recordings no longer freeze partway through on FFmpeg 8. Segmented renders with several workers start faster when media is slow to load, and long audio mixes do less work. @hyperframes/inspector no longer ships agent tools, so harnesses define their own.

Breaking Changes

  • Inspector: Stop shipping agent tools. Harnesses now define their own (abe97f6e4c, #5570). inspect_components, query_timeline, the stdio MCP server and the componentsTool, timelineTool, toolContent and InspectionTool exports from @hyperframes/inspector/live are gone. The HTTP contract (POST /inspect, /timeline, /element-map) is unchanged, and InspectRequest and TimelineRequest are now exported so a harness can build its own schema.

Fixes

  • Engine: Renders under WSL use the GPU through full Chrome when the headless shell cannot (9b996059af, #5574). It used to fall back to software rendering.
  • Producer: Start segmented render workers together so slow media waits overlap (d77b03c24c, #5573). Each worker used to wait for the one before it to finish loading media.
  • Engine: Sample VFR video by timestamp so it does not freeze on FFmpeg 8 (6afcb48395, #5572). FFmpeg 8 honours frame durations, so screen recordings with long, overlapping frames held one frame and dropped the rest. Cached frames from older versions are re-extracted.
  • Engine: Avoid padding every audio mix input (3de4763d53, #5563). Short clips no longer stay in the mix for the whole composition, so audio work no longer grows with clip count times length.

Internal

  • Studio: Run the edit accuracy slice on PRs and the full grid in the merge queue (9a2c1c6e80, #5566).

Full changelog

HyperFrames v0.8.155

Released on 2026-10-13.

MP4 renders at widths like 1000, 1080 or 1112 no longer get a black strip down the right edge on newer FFmpeg. Both the Studio render route and the producer render server now take encoder settings such as CRF, and distributed renders keep the CRF you ask for.

  • Producer: Keep the requested CRF in the distributed constant-frame-rate re-encode (bf4cf860fb, #5557). It used to fall back to the quality preset.

  • Runtime: Graded pictures stay graded in sandboxed players (684c03848, #5383).

HyperFrames v0.8.143

Released on 2026-10-08.

Distributed renders of long videos start much sooner. Each chunk now extracts only the video frames it shows, instead of the plan step extracting every frame up front. On AWS Lambda, a 26-minute clip now plans in about 20 seconds instead of over 6 minutes.

This release also fixes WebVTT caption parsing, makes hyperframes check and lint more accurate, and fixes SDK save and patch edge cases.

Fixes

  • Player: Honor runtime discovery and source in embeds (2dd708e0a, #5244).
  • SDK: Preserve unquoted escapes in inline styles (2df897aa4, #5246).
  • CLI: Normalize the audio passage the clip plays (1449d0d2a, #5222).
  • CLI: Preserve literal WebVTT cue text (1fac5fb29, #5236).
  • CLI: Bound timeline bars for negative media starts (83b2f5608, #5239).
  • CLI: Audit text beneath transparent composition boxes (b32ce10b7, #5202).
  • CLI: Recognize ancestor gradient text masks (f802aedb5, #5207).
  • CLI: Route timeline project directories to inspection (ee64ebe33, #5240).
  • CLI: Honor authored durations when listing compositions (1094b8ef0, #5265).
  • CLI: Preserve speaker labels in WebVTT cue text (7faff8154, #5233).
  • Lint: Parse inline script type and source attributes (9111d9f97, #5220).
  • Lint: Read attribute values with the HTML parser (b4c847aca, #5209).
  • Lint: Detect optional managed media calls (c03aa9224, #5210).
  • Core: Seek current dotLottie players by frame (c94d99218, #5275).
  • Slideshow: Validate nested hotspot entries (00729a566, #5211).
  • Core: Associate GIF delays with their image frames (e57d8178c, #5272).
  • CLI: Validate the complete TTS speed argument (5a7ada63b, #5264).
  • CLI: Preserve caption text inside script blocks (c9c9f4d36, #5226).
  • CLI: Retain WebVTT timestamps before cue settings (f5aeecdbf, #5224).
  • CLI: Encode background-removal WebM colors as BT.709 (2295ed5ea, #5278).
  • CLI: Reuse duplicate Figma nodes within asset batches (072de48e0, #5276).
  • CLI: Recover stale media cache entries (b1aa71d7d, #5269).
  • CLI: Preserve voice placement when ducking empty transcripts (320de3973, #5271).
  • CLI: Select media streams before reading adopted metadata (e6e5f68eb, #5270).
  • CLI: Report snapshot contact sheet failures (c9ddbd2d4, #5196).
  • CLI: Explain hardware GPU screenshot fallback (85360f370, #5200).
  • CLI: Close unused download responses before following redirects (037f73128, #5261).
  • Engine: Invalidate cached media metadata after file changes (730a33080, #5258).
  • CLI: Serve empty project assets without a stream error (58b7a4662, #5234).
  • CLI: Validate cached versions in update metadata (b407178f3, #5214).
  • SDK: Decode scoped IDs when replaying patches (548426fef, #5243).
  • Engine: Preserve out-of-range HDR object positions (95d5494ba, #5266).
  • Engine: Restore discarded warmup timing samples (971e1373b, #5204).
  • SDK: Preserve fragments with inert document markers (ea033bcd5, #5219).
  • SDK: Drain pending saves and adapter storage on flush (8efd9ca52, #5285).
  • Skills: Preserve preset color roles in frame contrast checks (29b901dc6, #5195).
  • Core: Test the minimum font size when fitting text (bb05bbe14, #5283).
  • Core: Read music sources through the shared HTML scanner (f478fa6ff, #5281).
  • AWS Lambda: Preserve null audio in CDK v2 assembly (006f87d1f, #5262).
  • Studio: Stop file names with %, apostrophes or $ from breaking Studio (621ddd469, #5156).

Performance

  • Producer: Distributed renders now extract each video's frames inside the chunks that show it, instead of all at once in the plan step (04f2bcd67, #5290).
  • Engine: Long videos are extracted in segments, and plan uploads start while extraction is still running (de1ef5a05, #5280).

HyperFrames v0.8.141

Released on 2026-10-08.

Renders no longer fail when a page links a Google font with axis values the family lacks. Studio previews of hard-to-play videos decode at their on-screen size.

Changes

  • A font whose Google Fonts link returns no usable faces now falls back to the standard weight request, so renders keep the font instead of failing. (#5186).
  • Unresolved-font errors carry structured diagnostics about which resolver step failed, without font names, URLs or page text. (#5189).
  • The player loads compositions using the document's own duration and reports the first author error. (#5176).
  • Studio decodes HEVC and ProRes previews at the size they appear on screen, so back-to-back 4K clips no longer flash the background. (#5184).
  • media-use can reach HeyGen through a host app's gateway with HEYGEN_API_BASE. (#5181).

item.title: v0.8.140
item.description:
HyperFrames v0.8.140

Released on 2026-10-07.

Motion blur now works over video, and rendering reports encoding and assembly progress. Studio previews, image replacement, and long-timeline zoom are more reliable.

Changes

  • Composition hosts can show the hover outline and set the stage’s starting size. (#5116).
  • Replacing an image fill now changes the displayed picture. (#5170).
  • Rebound root timelines keep advancing with the playback clock. (#5165).
  • Slow documents wait for their own frame cadence before capture. (#5168).
  • Fresh timeline updates from a host are preserved. (#5159).
  • Transcription keeps words spoken before the detected speech onset. (#5164).
  • Zooming long timelines does less image decoding and drawing. (#5142).
  • The preview catches up after missed file changes. (#5126).
  • Music requests use the host app’s music tools, with a clear error when the required CLI is missing. (#5154).
  • Feedback can report missing features and host-app friction without a rating. (#5140).
  • Automatic render worker counts respect the available memory budget. (#5149).
  • CLI startup loads reporting code without loading the full rendering engine, and history tests no longer race. (#5153).
  • Motion blur renders correctly over video by keeping the video frame steady across samples. (#5150).
  • Checks avoid false static-motion and text-overlap warnings on valid compositions. (#5147).
  • Imported scenes stay within their source time ranges. (#5132).
  • Rendering shows progress while encoding and assembling the output. (#5137).
  • Imported film HTML can use native capture while preserving its structure. (#5131).
  • Catalog previews run block scripts inline, and six shader blocks have dedicated documentation pages. (#5139).
  • The catalog adds six WebGPU shader backgrounds. (#5138).
  • Asynchronous frame sources can render repeatable frames. (#5130).
  • Skill publishing verifies that the latest creative guidance is available. (#5081).
  • WebGPU compositions can render with software graphics through an opt-in setting. (#5133).
  • Producer unit tests run without reaching the network. (#5135).
  • Timeline zoom stays smoother on long projects. (#5109).
  • Browser tests use a consistent launch path and a bounded time budget. (#5134).
  • The preview preloads upcoming scene images, and checks handle image swaps correctly. (#5128).

HyperFrames v0.8.139

Released on 2026-10-06.

Built-in transcription now runs inside the HyperFrames desktop app. transcribe --json streams words as they are heard, except with parakeet-mlx. Studio drags after a resize, undo or reload land where they were pressed.

Features

  • CLI: Stream heard words on the transcribe --json progress stream (156e87766, #5127).

Fixes

  • CLI: Read the WAV in JS so Built-in transcription runs inside Electron (f7bba2288, #5129).
  • Core: Keep nested scenes in place during a drag when the root has no timeline (d94708e53, #5115).
  • Core: Renders keep a fromTo's from-only values from the frame it starts on (755ab7d16, #5125).
  • Studio: Drags after a resize, undo or reload land where they were pressed (dc244d765, #5088).
  • CLI: Let parakeet-mlx detect the language and name the Parakeet install under auto (34552a21d, #5124).
  • Studio: A timeline jump no longer starts thumbnail loads it is about to cancel (b9e511a76, #5085).

Performance

  • Studio: Parse saved HTML once when syncing timeline length (e8cfd6b73, #5092).

Catalog

  • Registry: Gooey split block with metaball goo and directional motion blur (b50dead1d, #5123).
